key_insight: Quantum simulations designed to compute response functions also prepare many-body states that reveal how information spreads, can be read out, and becomes entangled.
engineering_relevance: Existing response-simulation protocols could support broader quantum-information diagnostics without redesigning state preparation, although useful readout depends on the model and measurements.
method: Study local-pulse Green-function protocols in finite XX and XXX spin chains.
Encode a classical bit with opposite source rotations and track its propagation and local accessibility.
Compare covariance-based reconstruction with spin measurements, and analyze estimation, communication, and entanglement.
evidence_signal: In the studied chains, fermionic covariance data exactly reconstruct the signed XX response, yet simple spin measurements recover a larger fraction of locally available information in XXX, an ordering that also holds for source-angle estimation.
watch_item: Results concern finite spin chains; scalability and robustness to experimental noise are not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information
